key_insight: BioScore evaluates whether pathology AI models capture biologically meaningful cell identities—not just whether they perform well on prediction tasks. It uses spatial transcriptomics from the same tissue as a biological reference.
problem_solved: Classification and retrieval benchmarks measure model usefulness but do not reveal how well a model's internal representations reflect tissue biology.
method: Extract tissue-image patch embeddings with a pathology image encoder.
Use a sparse autoencoder to decompose those embeddings into sparse features.
Assess how well the representations capture cell identities using spatial transcriptomics from the same tissue as a reference.
impact: BioScore offers practitioners a biology-grounded way to compare pathology foundation models alongside conventional task metrics. The provided abstract is truncated, so specific scoring details and experimental results cannot be summarized.
visual_elements: Side-by-side tissue image and spatial transcriptomics map showing the paired biological reference.
Pipeline diagram: image patches → encoder embeddings → sparse autoencoder features → biological evaluation.
Cell-type icons illustrating the biological identities the benchmark aims to assess.
Comparison graphic contrasting task performance with biological representation quality, without invented results.
paper_title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
paper_authors: Paul Vilars, Vincent Quoc-Huy Trinh, Maria Vakalopoulou, Dimitris Samaras, Stergios Christodoulidis
